title: Majestic Bishops
reviewNotes: Verified Black-to-move bishop underpromotion, queen/rook stalemates, the drawing knight promotion, and checking before capturing White’s bishop.
transcript: Of course we'd start with D2. We're only one step away from getting a new queen. But white is not just going to sit there and watch us get a new queen. Instead, he has a brilliant move to stop us. The incredible bishop to E1, sacrificing the last piece that he has on the board. But of course if we take the bishop now after king takes, we can't checkmate with only one bishop left. And actually, although it seems like we can get a queen, this would lead to a surprising stalemate. The white king is not checkmated, but there are no legal moves since the bishop is pinned to the king. So this is a draw. But if we don't move the pawn, on the next move white is just going to capture it, and that is also going to be a draw. So is black simply out of the woods? Well, not exactly. You see, we have the option of promoting to any one of these three other pieces. And one of them is going to allow us to win this game. Getting a knight seems to work at first because if white is not careful and for example goes to H4, we now actually have a check. And if the king moves here, this is a surprising checkmate. While if it moves on the other direction, we now have a discovered attack with the bishop, meaning that we can pick up the other bishop and win the game. But unfortunately, this does not work because if white is a good player, they're going to play bishop to A5. And now the bishop is simply out of the reach of the knight. So this would be yet again a draw. So incredibly, the only winning promotion is that to a bishop. And we'll end in this unreal position where every piece is a bishop. and the only legal move that white has is to move his own bishop. But if he's not careful and plays for example something like bishop to C3, now after bishop F2, the king is completely trapped and since this is a dark-squared bishop, it has no influence on the light-squared bishop coming to E2, which means that black would be able to checkmate like this. But white has not run out of ideas quite yet. And as a matter of fact, he has another brilliant move planned. The majestic bishop to F2, trying to give up the bishop yet again because this time if black takes, this is going to be another draw. But luckily for white, it is enough to give a check first, force the king to move and after we collect his bishop, this is going to be enough to force a double bishop beautiful checkmate.
